what_its_for: Theophylline is used to treat and prevent breathing problems caused by asthma, chronic bronchitis, and emphysema (also called COPD). It works by relaxing the muscles around your airways, making it easier to breathe. It also helps reduce swelling in your airways.
how_to_take: Take this medicine exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow extended-release tablets or capsules whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. You may take theophylline with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time (always with food or always without food) since food can affect how much medicine your body absorbs. If you take a capsule form, you may carefully open it and sprinkle the contents on a spoonful of soft food like applesauce, but swallow it right away without chewing.
dosing: Your dose is carefully calculated based on your weight, age, other medical conditions, and other medicines you take. Do NOT change your dose on your own. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to check your theophylline level and make sure it stays in a safe range. Typical doses for adults are often taken once or twice daily for extended-release forms, but your doctor will give you your specific dosing schedule. Always follow your personal prescription label.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — UNLESS it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one, as this can lead to dangerous levels of medicine in your blood.
storage: Store theophylline at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use medicine that is past its expiration date. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking cigarettes or marijuana, as smoking makes this medicine work less effectively. Avoid large amounts of caffeine (coffee, tea, energy drinks, chocolate), since caffeine can increase side effects like fast heartbeat, shakiness, and trouble sleeping. Avoid starting or stopping a high-protein or high-carbohydrate diet without telling your doctor, as changes in your diet can affect how this medicine works. Let your doctor and pharmacist know before taking any new prescription or over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements, because many common medications interact with theophylline. Avoid charbroiled or grilled meats regularly, as they can also affect drug levels.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain; fast, irregular, or pounding heartbeat; seizures; severe headache; feeling restless, irritable, or very shaky; muscle twitching; or confusion. These may be signs that you have too much theophylline in your body, which is a serious medical emergency. Also call your doctor if your breathing does not improve or gets worse.
when_it_works: Extended-release forms of theophylline are designed to work over a long period of time (12 to 24 hours) to keep your airways open throughout the day and night. You may not feel immediate relief right away. This medicine is used for long-term prevention and control of breathing problems — it is NOT a rescue inhaler for sudden breathing attacks. Always use your quick-relief rescue inhaler (if prescribed) for sudden breathing problems.
special_populations: Older adults (65+) are more sensitive to theophylline and may need lower doses. Children require doses carefully calculated by weight and age. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should discuss the risks and benefits with their doctor before using this medicine, as theophylline can pass into breast milk. People with heart disease, liver disease, thyroid problems, or a history of seizures should use this medicine with extra caution and closer monitoring. People who smoke need higher doses because smoking speeds up how fast the body removes this medicine; if you quit smoking, tell your doctor right away so your dose can be adjusted.
